title: Outlook for Mac: sensitivity label inheritance from email attachments
summary: Hold: the briefing says the applicable licence level is unpublished, although the cited service description gives a requirement for automatic or policy-based sensitivity labeling. The portal paths and PowerShell settings are supported, and the Mac release notes still disagree with the capabilities table as the briefing reports.

claims.claim: Roadmap item 569022 concerns Outlook for Mac applying or recommending an email sensitivity label based on attached files.
claims.quote: When composing an email in Outlook for Mac, Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels can be automatically applied or recommended based on the sensitivity labels of attached files.

claims.claim: The Purview route through Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies > policy > Edit Policy leads to the inheritance checkbox under Default settings for emails > Inherit label from attachments.
claims.quote: You configure this setting in the sensitivity label policy, on the Default settings for emails page. For the section Inherit label from attachments, select the checkbox Email inherits highest priority label from attachments.

claims.claim: Set-LabelPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AdvancedSettings @{AttachmentAction="Automatic"} configures automatic attachment-label inheritance.
claims.quote: AttachmentAction: Unlabeled emails inherit the highest priority label from file attachments. Set the value to Automatic (to automatically apply the label) ... Example: Set-LabelPolicy -Identity Global -AdvancedSettings @{AttachmentAction="Automatic"}.

claims.claim: The same Purview policy-editing route leads to Recommend users apply the attachments label instead of automatically applying it under the inheritance section.
claims.quote: When you select this checkbox, you can then further select the following option: Recommend users apply the attachments label instead of automatically applying it.

claims.claim: Set-LabelPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AdvancedSettings @{AttachmentAction="Recommended"} configures recommendation of the attachment label.
claims.quote: AttachmentAction: Unlabeled emails inherit the highest priority label from file attachments. Set the value to Automatic (to automatically apply the label) or Recommended (as a recommended prompt to the user.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The service description does not separately name label inheritance from email attachments in a licensing row.
claims.quote: Searched: 'label inheritance from email attachments licensing E3 E5', 'AttachmentAction license', 'label inheritance E3', 'label inheritance E5'; opened and searched the Purview service description and read its Information Protection licensing tables.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Which licence level covers attachment-label inheritance is not yet published.
claims.quote: Sensitivity labeling, including automatic or policy-based labeling, requires a Microsoft 365 E5 license or Microsoft 365 Information Protection and Governance (IPG).
claims.fix: Replace the unpublished-licence-level sentence with: 'The service description requires Microsoft 365 E5 or Microsoft 365 Information Protection and Governance (IPG) for automatic or policy-based sensitivity labeling; it does not name attachment inheritance separately.' Remove the open question asking whether the E3 manual-labeling row covers this feature, and replace 'which licence level covers it is not stated' in the cost rationale with 'the service description gives an E5 or IPG requirement for automatic or policy-based labeling'. Retain the narrower statement that no separate attachment-inheritance licensing row is published.

claims.claim: The service description publishes no meter specifically for attachment-label inheritance.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Outlook label inheritance attachments pricing meter licensing'; opened the Purview service description and get-started sensitivity-labels licensing/billing section, and searched the service description for inheritance and meter.

claims.claim: The service description publishes no price specifically for attachment-label inheritance.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Outlook label inheritance attachments pricing meter licensing'; opened the Purview service description, get-started sensitivity-labels licensing/billing section and Office-apps inheritance documentation; no feature-specific price was stated.

claims.claim: The roadmap description does not mention licensing.
claims.quote: This helps users consistently protect sensitive information, reduces manual labeling effort, and supports organizational compliance requirements by aligning email protection with the sensitivity of attached content.

claims.claim: Using sensitivity labels in Office apps requires a subscription edition of Office.
claims.quote: To use sensitivity labels in Office apps, you must use a subscription edition of Office.

claims.claim: Outlook for Mac supports sensitivity labels for on-premises mailboxes starting with version 16.112.
claims.quote: For Outlook for Mac, sensitivity labels are supported for on-premises mailboxes starting with version 16.112.

claims.quote:
You can use the following role groups:
Information Protection
Information Protection Admins
Information Protection Analysts
Information Protection Investigators
Information Protection Readers

claims.claim: Microsoft has not explicitly stated whether an already-enabled inheritance policy starts applying to Mac users when they update.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Outlook Mac AttachmentAction existing policy update enabled label inheritance'; read Office-apps inheritance settings, Set-LabelPolicy, policy publication/editing, Mac release notes and capabilities table. None explicitly describes this Mac-update transition.

claims.claim: Email-label-based mail-flow, DLP and encryption controls can operate on the label inherited from attachments.
claims.quote: Any mail-flow or DLP related controls that are tied to the email's label ... is applied based on the email's attachments. ... If the inherited label includes any advanced controls, such as label encryption, the email has these controls applied
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/compliance/anz/pspf-label-publishing#label-inheritance to sources for the existing mail-flow and DLP applicability statement.

claims.claim: Recipients not authorized by an inherited label's encryption permissions may be unable to open the email.
claims.quote: When a document, email, or meeting invite is encrypted, access to the content is restricted ... Can be decrypted only by users authorized by the label's encryption settings.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/encryption-sensitivity-labels to sources for the existing statement about recipients being unable to open encrypted emails.

claims.claim: Information Protection > Sensitivity labels identifies the label list used to review label scopes.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels
claims.fix: Replace the parenthetical route with 'Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels'.

claims.claim: Files-and-emails scope is configured on a sensitivity label rather than on the publishing policy.
claims.quote: On the Define the scope for this label page, the options selected determine the label's scope for the settings that you can configure and where they'll be visible when they're published

claims.claim: Label ordering is configurable at the label level and determines priority for selecting an inherited attachment label.
claims.quote: When you've created all the labels you need, review their order and if necessary, move them up or down. ... For more information, see Label priority (order matters)

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The checklist asks readers to review label publication, scopes, priority and encryption, but the controls table has no rows for those controls.
claims.quote: Check which labels are published to Mac users and confirm each is scoped to both files and emails ... Review label priority order ... List the labels that apply encryption; table: only inheritance and recommendation.
claims.fix: The label-publication, label-scope, label-priority and encryption review steps have no corresponding control rows. Remove the first three Before rollout checklist bullets; do not add control rows.

claims.claim: A custom role group containing Sensitivity Label Administrator is another route for configuring labels and policies.
claims.quote: Alternatively to using the default role groups, you can create a new role group and add the Sensitivity Label Administrator role to this group.

claims.claim: Compliance Data Administrator, Compliance Administrator or Security Administrator role groups are alternative permission routes.
claims.quote: Another option is to add users to the Compliance Data Administrator, Compliance Administrator, or Security Administrator role group.

claims.claim: Learn's attachment-inheritance examples for Double Key Encryption explicitly describe Outlook for Windows.
claims.quote: When Outlook doesn't support DKE: If the highest priority label applies Double Key Encryption, no label or encryption is selected for the email message in Outlook for Windows.
